statement: In log-rate coordinates a strictly supported pair is below the sharp reverse-exponential bound.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {ξ u v d s : ℝ} (hξ : ξ ∈ Icc (-1 : ℝ) 1) (hu : 0 ≤ u) (hd : 0 < d) (hs : 0 < s) (hgap : d = 2 * s * exp (-ξ * v) * distanceFactor ξ u) : -2 * log s + 2 * (1 + ξ) * v - (exp (v + u) + exp (v - u)) < 2 * (log 2 - 1 - log d)

statement: A reverse-exponential pair ties the bound exactly at upper contact with half-gap scale.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {d s gap : ℝ} (hd : 0 < d) (hs : 0 < s) (hg : 0 ≤ gap) : -2 * log s - (d + 2 * gap) / s ≤ 2 * (log 2 - 1 - log d) ∧ (-2 * log s - (d + 2 * gap) / s = 2 * (log 2 - 1 - log d) ↔ gap = 0 ∧ s = d / 2)

statement: At exact half minimum multiplicity the fitted supremum equals the collapse value. Its finite equality cases are exactly the balanced two-value reverse-exponential fits.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) {x : Fin n → ℝ} {m : ℝ} (hm : ∀ i, m ≤ x i) (hc : n = 2 * Frechet.minimumCount (GEV.lowerGaps x m)) : let D : Set (ℝ × (ℝ × ℝ)) := {q | q.1 ∈ Icc (-1 : ℝ) 1 ∧ q.2 ∈ GEV.domain x q.1} let L := fun q : ℝ × (ℝ × ℝ) ↦ GEV.logLik x q.1 q.2 let A := (n : ℝ) * (log 2 - 1) - 2 * ∑ i, log (x i - m) IsLUB (L '' D) A ∧ (∀ q ∈ D, L q = A ↔ q.1 = -1 ∧ ∀ j, m < x j → q.2.1 + q.2.2 = x j ∧ q.2.2 = (x j - m) / 2) ∧ ((∃ q ∈ D, IsMaxOn L D q) ↔ ∃ d > 0, ∀ j, m < x j → x j - m = d)

statement: The unrestricted fit is unbounded. The fitted branch diverges at majority contact and has the sharp finite collapse supremum at half contact, with the balanced two-value exception.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (x : Fin n → ℝ) : let D : Set (ℝ × (ℝ × ℝ)) := {q | q.1 ∈ Icc (-1 : ℝ) 1 ∧ q.2 ∈ GEV.domain x q.1} let L := fun q : ℝ × (ℝ × ℝ) ↦ GEV.logLik x q.1 q.2 (¬ BddAbove {v | ∃ ξ : ℝ, ∃ p ∈ GEV.domain x ξ, GEV.logLik x ξ p = v}) ∧ ∀ m : ℝ, (∀ i, m ≤ x i) → (∃ i, x i = m) → let k := Frechet.minimumCount (GEV.lowerGaps x m) let A := (n : ℝ) * (log 2 - 1) - 2 * ∑ i, log (x i - m) (n < 2 * k → Tendsto (fun e ↦ GEV.logLik x 1 (GEV.collapsePath x m 1 e)) (𝓝[>] 0) atTop ∧ ¬ BddAbove (L '' D) ∧ ¬ ∃ q ∈ D, IsMaxOn L D q) ∧ (n = 2 * k → Tendsto (fun e ↦ GEV.logLik x 1 (GEV.collapsePath x m 1 e)) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 A) ∧ IsLUB (L '' D) A ∧ ((∃ q ∈ D, IsMaxOn L D q) ↔ ∃ d > 0, ∀ j, m < x j → x j - m = d))

statement: Uniform density envelopes give a scale bound, a quadratic distance bound and arbitrary polynomial left-tail decay.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {ξ x : ℝ} {p : ℝ × ℝ} (hξ : ξ ∈ Icc (-1 : ℝ) 1) (hs : 0 < p.2) (ha : if ξ = -1 then 0 ≤ GEV.supportArg ξ x p else 0 < GEV.supportArg ξ x p) : logCell ξ x p ≤ -log p.2 + 2 * log 2 ∧ (x ≠ p.1 → logCell ξ x p ≤ log p.2 + 2 * log 2 - 1 - 2 * log |x - p.1|) ∧ (∀ N : ℕ, x < p.1 → logCell ξ x p ≤ -log p.2 + (N + 2 : ℝ) * log (N + 2) - (N : ℝ) * log ((p.1 - x) / p.2)) := ⟨logCell_near hξ ha, fun h ↦ logCell_far hξ hs h ha, fun N h ↦ logCell_left N hξ hs h ha⟩ private theorem logLik_large {n : ℕ} (x : Fin n → ℝ) {ξ : ℝ} {p : ℝ × ℝ} (hξ : ξ ∈ Icc (-1 : ℝ) 1) (hp : p ∈ GEV.domain x ξ) : GEV.logLik x ξ p ≤ (n : ℝ) * (-log p.2 + 2 * log 2)

statement: The joint fitted likelihood extended by zero is upper semicontinuous at positive scale.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {n : ℕ} (x : Fin n → ℝ) : UpperSemicontinuousOn (likelihood x) chart

statement: An attained strict minimum minority gives compact free physical likelihood superlevels.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) {x : Fin n → ℝ} {m : ℝ} (hm : ∀ i, m ≤ x i) (hz : ∃ i, x i = m) (hk : 2 * Frechet.minimumCount (GEV.lowerGaps x m) < n) {e : ℝ} (he : 0 < e) : IsCompact (chart ∩ likelihood x ⁻¹' Ici e)

statement: With location held, a negative residual or a strict zero minority gives compact positive superlevels.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) {x : Fin n → ℝ} {m : ℝ} (h : (∃ i, x i < m) ∨ 2 * Frechet.minimumCount (GEV.lowerGaps x m) < n) {e : ℝ} (he : 0 < e) : IsCompact ((chart ∩ {q : Parameters | q.2.1 = m}) ∩ likelihood x ⁻¹' Ici e)

statement: A fitted maximum exists exactly at strict minority contact or for a balanced two-value sample at half contact.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) {x : Fin n → ℝ} {m : ℝ} (hm : ∀ i, m ≤ x i) (hz : ∃ i, x i = m) : let k := Frechet.minimumCount (GEV.lowerGaps x m) (∃ q ∈ domain x, IsMaxOn (fun r ↦ GEV.logLik x r.1 r.2) (domain x) q) ↔ 2 * k < n ∨ (n = 2 * k ∧ ∃ d > 0, ∀ i, m < x i → x i - m = d)

statement: With location held, a fitted maximum exists with a negative residual or strict zero minority, or at nonnegative half contact with all positive residuals equal.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) {x : Fin n → ℝ} (m : ℝ) : let k := Frechet.minimumCount (GEV.lowerGaps x m) let D : Set (ℝ × ℝ) := {p | p.1 ∈ Icc (-1 : ℝ) 1 ∧ (m, p.2) ∈ GEV.domain x p.1} let L := fun p : ℝ × ℝ ↦ GEV.logLik x p.1 (m, p.2) (∃ p ∈ D, IsMaxOn L D p) ↔ (∃ i, x i < m) ∨ 2 * k < n ∨ ((∀ i, m ≤ x i) ∧ n = 2 * k ∧ ∃ d > 0, ∀ i, m < x i → x i - m = d)

statement: At positive reciprocal shape the GEV-seam profile equals the original Fréchet nuisance supremum.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {n : ℕ} {g : Fin n → ℝ} (hg : ∀ i, 0 ≤ g i) (hz : ∃ i, g i = 0) {b : ℝ} (hb : 0 < b) : profile g b = sSup {v | ∃ p ∈ Frechet.domain, Frechet.logLik g b⁻¹ p.1 p.2 = v}

statement: A strict minimum minority gives compact superlevels of the extended reciprocal-shape profile.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) {g : Fin n → ℝ} (hg : ∀ i, 0 ≤ g i) (hz : ∃ i, g i = 0) (hk : 2 * Frechet.minimumCount g < n) (v : ℝ) : IsCompact (Icc (0 : ℝ) 1 ∩ profile g ⁻¹' Ici v)

statement: A strict minimum minority gives continuity of the extended profile including its optimized Gumbel seam.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) {g : Fin n → ℝ} (hg : ∀ i, 0 ≤ g i) (hz : ∃ i, g i = 0) (hk : 2 * Frechet.minimumCount g < n) : ContinuousOn (profile g) (Icc (0 : ℝ) 1)

statement: The unrestricted likelihood is unbounded. On the fitted branch a maximum exists exactly at strict minimum minority with a positive reciprocal shape reaching optimized Gumbel.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) {g : Fin n → ℝ} (hg : ∀ i, 0 ≤ g i) (hz : ∃ i, g i = 0) : (¬ BddAbove {v | ∃ a > 0, ∃ p ∈ Frechet.domain, Frechet.logLik g a p.1 p.2 = v}) ∧ ((∃ v, IsGreatest (fittedValues g) v) ↔ 2 * Frechet.minimumCount g < n ∧ ∃ b ∈ Ioc (0 : ℝ) 1, profile g 0 ≤ profile g b)

statement: Majority ties diverge. Half ties give a strict finite collapse bound above Gumbel. With a strict minority, Gumbel is the unattained supremum exactly when all positive reciprocal shapes lose.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) {g : Fin n → ℝ} (hg : ∀ i, 0 ≤ g i) (hz : ∃ i, g i = 0) : let k := Frechet.minimumCount g let A := (n : ℝ) * (log 2 - 1) - 2 * ∑ i, log (g i) (n < 2 * k → ¬ BddAbove (fittedValues g)) ∧ (n = 2 * k → IsLUB (fittedValues g) A ∧ (∀ v ∈ fittedValues g, v < A) ∧ Tendsto (Frechet.profile g 1) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 A) ∧ profile g 0 < A) ∧ (2 * k < n → ((∀ b ∈ Ioc (0 : ℝ) 1, profile g b < profile g 0) ↔ IsLUB (fittedValues g) (profile g 0) ∧ ¬ ∃ v, IsGreatest (fittedValues g) v))

statement: At fixed shape and scale, the conditional exponent is optimized by n divided by the transformed loss sum.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {x : Fin n → ℝ} (hn : 0 < n) (hx : ∀ i, 0 < x i) {b a m : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a) : let d : Fin n → ℝ := fun i ↦ log (x i) - m let u := exp (b * (m - log a)) let c₀ := (n : ℝ) / H d b u 0 < c₀ ∧ ShapeFacesExpWeibull.logLik x b a c₀ = jointProfile d b u - ∑ i, log (x i) ∧ ∀ c > 0, ShapeFacesExpWeibull.logLik x b a c ≤ ShapeFacesExpWeibull.logLik x b a c₀

statement: On any compact positive shape interval the joint exponent-profiled superlevels are compact.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {d : Fin n → ℝ} (hd : ∀ i, 0 ≤ d i) (hne : ∃ i, 0 < d i) {j : Fin n} (hj : d j = 0) {a B v : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a) : IsCompact ((Icc a B ×ˢ Ioi (0 : ℝ)) ∩ (fun p : ℝ × ℝ ↦ jointProfile d p.1 p.2) ⁻¹' Ici v)

statement: At large shape the optimized closed power value bounds the joint profile up to arbitrary tolerance, uniformly over scale.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {d : Fin n → ℝ} {D : ℝ} (hd : ∀ i, d i ≤ D) (hD : 0 < D) {j l : Fin n} (hj : d j = 0) (hl : d l = D) {v : ℝ} (hv : powerValue d D < v) : ∀ᶠ b : ℝ in atTop, ∀ u > 0, jointProfile d b u < v

statement: At small shape the optimized inverse-Weibull value bounds the joint profile up to arbitrary tolerance, uniformly over scale.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {d : Fin n → ℝ} (hd : ∀ i, 0 ≤ d i) (hne : ∃ i, 0 < d i) {j : Fin n} (hj : d j = 0) {I v : ℝ} (hI : ∀ k > 0, inverseProfile d k ≤ I) (hv : I < v) : ∀ᶠ b : ℝ in 𝓝[>] 0, ∀ u > 0, jointProfile d b u < v

statement: The optimized shape profile converges to the optimal inverse-Weibull and closed power values at the respective ends, including tied upper contacts.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {x : Fin n → ℝ} (hn : 0 < n) (hx : ∀ i, 0 < x i) (hne : ∃ i j, x i ≠ x j) {M : ℝ} (hM : ∀ i, log (x i) ≤ M) (htop : ∃ i, log (x i) = M) : ∃ p ∈ Weibull.domain, IsMaxOn (fun q : ℝ × ℝ ↦ Weibull.Inverse.logLik x q.1 q.2) Weibull.domain p ∧ Tendsto (shapeProfile x) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 (Weibull.Inverse.logLik x p.1 p.2)) ∧ Tendsto (shapeProfile x) atTop (𝓝 (physicalPowerValue x M))

statement: Constants are unbounded. On nonconstant data a maximum exists exactly when a finite point reaches the better face. If all finite points lose, the better face is the unattained supremum with both labels valid at equal heights.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {x : Fin n → ℝ} (hn : 0 < n) (hx : ∀ i, 0 < x i) {M : ℝ} (hM : ∀ i, log (x i) ≤ M) (htop : ∃ i, log (x i) = M) : let N := ∃ i j, x i ≠ x j (¬ N → ¬ BddAbove (finiteValues x) ∧ ¬ ∃ v, IsGreatest (finiteValues x) v) ∧ (N → ∃ p ∈ Weibull.domain, IsMaxOn (fun q : ℝ × ℝ ↦ Weibull.Inverse.logLik x q.1 q.2) Weibull.domain p ∧ let I := Weibull.Inverse.logLik x p.1 p.2 let P := physicalPowerValue x M BddAbove (finiteValues x) ∧ ((∃ v, IsGreatest (finiteValues x) v) ↔ ∃ v ∈ finiteValues x, max I P ≤ v) ∧ ((∀ v ∈ finiteValues x, v < max I P) ↔ IsLUB (finiteValues x) (max I P) ∧ ¬ ∃ v, IsGreatest (finiteValues x) v) ∧ ((∀ v ∈ finiteValues x, v < max I P) → (IsLUB (finiteValues x) I ↔ P ≤ I) ∧ (IsLUB (finiteValues x) P ↔ I ≤ P)))
